1. Core Clinical Tension: A 50-year-old rural woman presenting with a recurrent, slowly enlarging, painful soft-tissue mass of the lower extremity adjacent to a prior surgical scar, raising the differential of soft-tissue sarcoma, intramuscular abscess/myositis, or recurrent parasitic cystic disease without concomitant pulmonary or hepatic involvement.
2. Admission Breakpoint: Presentation and diagnostic imaging workup including leg radiography, magnetic resonance imaging showing multilocular subcutaneous and deep intramuscular cystic collections, normal chest radiography, normal abdominal ultrasonography, and baseline routine laboratory results, prior to serological parasite testing, pre-operative antihelmintic therapy, and surgical re-excision.
3. Differential Distinctions: Soft-tissue sarcoma / cystic mesenchymal neoplasm (e.g., synovial sarcoma, myxoid liposarcoma) typically presents as an enlarging painless or painful mass near neurovascular bundles but does not form well-defined, scalloped, multi-chambered fluid cysts following prior benign cyst excision; pyogenic or cold bacterial/mycobacterial abscess is ruled out by normal CBC/electrolytes, lack of erythema or systemic signs; musculoskeletal hydatid disease exhibits thick scalloped enhancing capsules in endemic rural settings, positive serology, and pathognomonic laminated cyst walls on histopathology.
case_prompt: A 50-year-old woman from rural Morocco presents with a two-year history of worsening pain and progressive swelling along the medial aspect of her right leg. She reports having undergone surgical excision of a subcutaneous cystic mass in the same anatomical region at another hospital three years prior, without receiving adjuvant medical therapy. She reports no antecedent trauma, fevers, or weight loss. On physical examination, a tender, non-erythematous 5 × 7 cm mass is palpated along the medial right leg adjacent to the previous surgical incision, with no evidence of neurovascular compromise. Plain radiography of the right leg reveals increased soft tissue density overlying the medial aspect of the tibia without bony destruction. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the lower extremity demonstrates a 52 × 28 × 72 mm subcutaneous fluid collection adjacent to the upper-to-middle medial tibial periosteum featuring a thick, scalloped, gadolinium-enhancing capsule, alongside a second 21 × 9 × 38 mm intramuscular cystic collection within the tibialis posterior muscle abutting the posterior tibial and peroneal vessels. Routine laboratory tests, including complete blood count and serum electrolytes, are within normal limits. A screening chest radiograph and abdominal ultrasound demonstrate no visceral lesions or abnormalities.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: A recurrent, enlarging deep muscular mass adjacent to major neurovascular structures in an adult patient strongly raises suspicion for a malignant soft-tissue neoplasm (such as synovial sarcoma or malignant fibrous histiocytoma); however, the multi-cystic fluid nature with well-defined scalloped walls and lack of invasive solid tissue proliferation on MRI, combined with positive parasite serology and surgical cyst walls, excluded a malignant tumor.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) revealed the presence of a subcutaneous collection in proximity to the medial surface of the tibia at the junction of his upper and middle third adherent to the periosteum with a thick and scalloped wall, enhanced after gadolinium injection and fluid filled measuring 52x28x72 mm and a second deep collection at the tibialis posterior muscle measuring 21x9x38 mm sitting in front of the posterior tibial and peroneal arteries (Figure 3).

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Chronic Pyogenic / Tuberculous Intramuscular Cold Abscess
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Chronic intramuscular fluid collections can represent pyogenic abscesses or tuberculous cold abscesses; however, the patient lacked systemic symptoms, fevers, or erythema, exhibited normal inflammatory and hematological labs, and showed clear fluid-filled encapsulated architecture rather than caseous suppurative tracking.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: No history of trauma, fever and weight loss was reported. A painful mass (Figure 1) next the previous incision was palpated on the medial side of the right leg; it was 5x7cm in diameter and there was no erythema and no sign of neurovascular compression

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The patient's epidemiological origin in rural Morocco, previous surgical resection of a subcutaneous cyst without adjuvant chemotherapy, typical MRI characteristics of multi-compartmental thick scalloped cystic collections, positive specific ELISA serology, and subsequent surgical pathology confirming hydatid membranes established the diagnosis of recurrent subcutaneous and muscular hydatidosis.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Complete blood count and electrolytes was normal, ELISA (Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay) test for echinococcosis was positive. The diagnosis of recurrent hydatidosis has been retained... Pathological examination of the cyst confirmed the diagnosis.

editor_comments: Follows Stanford MedCaseReasoning guidelines with complete fidelity. Case prompt captures clinical history, leg exam, MRI findings, and negative systemic screening without spoiling the parasite identity from the remote surgical history. Differential includes soft-tissue sarcoma and infectious cold abscess supported by direct textual quotes.
